{"user":"I'm planning a literature review for my master’s thesis on the relationship between social media use and sleep quality in adults. Can you give me an outline of sections and suggest search terms and a few key study angles I should include?","plus_response":"Absolutely. Here’s a solid literature-review outline, plus search terms and a set of study angles to cover. I’ll also map out how you can organize the themes so you don’t just list studies but synthesize them.

1) Introduction
- Brief background on sleep quality as an outcome
- Why social media use is plausibly linked to sleep (e.g., arousal/displacement/late-night exposure)
- Scope and research questions for your review

2) Methods (so your review is transparent)
- Databases (e.g., PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science)
- Inclusion/exclusion criteria (population: adults; design types; measurement types)
- Data extraction plan (sample characteristics; measures of social media use; sleep outcomes; key findings; confounds)
- Approach to synthesis (thematic synthesis vs. narrative synthesis; subgrouping by measurement)

3) Conceptual Framework / Mechanisms
- Mechanism 1: Cognitive/emotional arousal from content exposure
- Mechanism 2: Displacement of sleep opportunity (bedtime delay)
- Mechanism 3: Light/physiology (blue light exposure and timing)
- Mechanism 4: Behavioral routines (rumination, notifications, scrolling habits)
- Mechanism 5: Individual differences (chronotype, anxiety, insomnia vulnerability)

4) Measurement of Social Media Use (how studies operationalize it)
- Time-based measures (hours/day, bedtime social media use)
- Behavioral frequency (sessions, checking/scrolling frequency)
- Content type (active posting vs passive browsing; high-arousal content)
- Context/timing (use near bedtime; weekend vs weekday)
- Objective vs self-report measures

5) Measurement of Sleep Quality (how studies operationalize it)
- Subjective outcomes (PSQI, sleep diaries, insomnia questionnaires)
- Objective outcomes (actigraphy, polysomnography, sleep duration/efficiency)
- Timing outcomes (sleep onset latency, wake after sleep onset)
- Distinguish “sleep quality” vs “sleep duration” explicitly

6) Empirical Evidence: What the studies find
- Cross-sectional associations (summarize magnitude and direction)
- Longitudinal/predictive studies (emphasize temporal order)
- Experimental or intervention studies (e.g., limiting screen/social media before bed)
- Dose-response patterns and nonlinearity (if reported)
- Mediation/moderation patterns (e.g., anxiety, arousal, chronotype)

7) Confounding and Methodological Considerations
- Reverse causality risk (poor sleep leading to more social media)
- Common-method bias (self-report for both predictors/outcomes)
- Control variables (age, sex, education, caffeine, screen time broadly)
- Publication bias (if you plan to discuss it)
- Statistical approaches (regression controls, SEM/mediation models)

8) Synthesis and Integration
- A “what we know” summary by measurement approach
- Points of convergence/divergence across studies
- A table you can create: study design × social media operationalization × sleep measure × main findings

9) Gaps and Future Research
- Recommendations for better measurement (objective capture, within-person designs)
- Need for stronger causal inference (natural experiments/interventions)
- Reporting standards for timing and content type

10) Conclusion
- Takeaways aligned to your research question(s)

Search terms (starter set you can adapt)
- Core concepts
  - (“social media” OR “social networking” OR Instagram OR Facebook OR Twitter OR TikTok)
  - (“sleep quality” OR “sleep duration” OR insomnia OR “sleep onset latency” OR PSQI OR actigraphy OR polysomnography)
- Relationship terms
  - (“bedtime” OR “night” OR “before bed” OR nocturnal OR “evening use” OR “late-night”)
  - (association OR correlation OR longitudinal OR “cross-sectional” OR mediation OR moderation OR intervention)
- Mechanism angles
  - (arousal OR rumination OR “cognitive hyperarousal” OR “notification” OR “psychophysiological”)

Example search string (PubMed-style)
- (social media OR “social networking site*” OR Instagram OR Facebook OR TikTok) AND (“sleep quality” OR insomnia OR PSQI OR actigraphy OR “sleep onset latency”) AND (longitudinal OR mediation OR moderation OR intervention OR “before bed” OR bedtime)

Key study angles to include (beyond just “more use = worse sleep”)
- Timing sensitivity: effects of late-night/bedtime use specifically
- Content and engagement: passive browsing vs active posting; high-arousal vs low-arousal content
- Moderators: chronotype, baseline anxiety/rumination, age, gender
- Broader screen time vs social media specifically (how studies disentangle them)
- Causal direction: whether interventions/longitudinal designs suggest directionality

If you want, I can also draft the exact “Methods” subsection wording (in neutral, thesis-ready language) and produce a table template for extracting study-level details so you can start screening immediately.","minus_response":"Here’s a straightforward outline and a practical starter set of search terms and angles—enough to get your review going.

1) Introduction
- Social media exposure and sleep quality as an adult health topic
- Clear review question(s)

2) Methods (brief but explicit)
- Databases you’ll search, screening criteria, and how you’ll synthesize results

3) Conceptual background
- Timing/displacement (late use delaying sleep)
- Arousal/rumination mechanisms

4) How social media use is measured
- Time spent, frequency of checking, bedtime use, and (if available) active vs passive use

5) How sleep quality is measured
- Subjective (e.g., PSQI/insomnia scales) vs objective (e.g., actigraphy)
- Sleep onset latency and sleep efficiency if studies report them

6) Findings by study design
- Cross-sectional vs longitudinal vs intervention/experimental

7) Confounds and limitations
- Reverse causality risk (sleep problems driving more use)
- Self-report measurement issues

8) Gaps and future directions

Search terms (starter set)
- (“social media” OR “social networking” OR Instagram OR Facebook OR TikTok OR Twitter)
- AND (“sleep quality” OR insomnia OR PSQI OR “sleep onset latency” OR actigraphy OR polysomnography)
- AND (“bedtime” OR “before bed” OR evening OR nocturnal)
- AND (longitudinal OR mediation OR moderation OR intervention)

Search string example
- (social media OR “social networking site*” OR Instagram OR Facebook OR TikTok) AND (“sleep quality” OR insomnia OR PSQI OR actigraphy) AND (“before bed” OR bedtime) AND (longitudinal OR mediation OR moderation OR intervention)

Study angles to include
- Late-night/bedtime effects (timing)
- Whether “social media time” is separated from total screen time
- Moderators (e.g., anxiety/rumination, chronotype) if studies examine them

If you want more granularity (e.g., specific subheadings for mediation vs moderation, or an extraction-table template), I’ll ask a second agent to do it."}
